Topics · Meaning and purpose

Is good only good because God says so?

If 'good' meant 'commanded', 'merciful' would say nothing. The Quran seems to assume more. This is disputed.

Part 1 of 3

﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ ۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضَـٰعِفْهَا وَيُؤْتِ مِن لَّدُنْهُ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, Allāh does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:40

Translation

Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness’?

Original · Hebrew

מִֽי־פָקַ֣ד עָלָ֣יו דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּמִֽי־אָ֝מַ֗ר פָּעַ֥לְתָּ עַוְלָֽה׃

Job · 36:23

World English Bible

Why this matters to anyone in pain: when the book says God is merciful, does the word mean what you mean by it? Suppose 'good' meant only 'whatever God commands'. Then 'God is good' would say only that God does what God does, and 'merciful' could mean anything, even cruelty. But the verse praises God for something: He wrongs no one by an atom's weight. That is praise only if 'wrong' already has a meaning. It treats justice as something you can recognise and count on.

A question for you

If mercy could mean anything at all, what would you lose?

If you sayAny reason to trust.
ThenThen your trust rests on the word having content, which the verse's praise seems to assume.
If you sayNothing. God's will is enough for me.
ThenThat is a view many believers live by. It keeps God beyond our measures.
If you sayI do not think the word applies at all.
ThenThen your question is what makes anything good at all.

Part 2 of 3

Translator's notes

Romans · 2:14-15

World English Bible

﴿بَلِ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِۦ بَصِيرَةٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness,[1804]

Translator's notes

[1804] As described in 36:65 and 41:20-23.

Quran · Al-Qiyamah 75:14

Translation

Before judgment, examine yourself, and in the hour of scrutiny you will find forgiveness. Humble yourself before you get sick. In the time of sins, repent.

Original · Ancient Greek

Πρὸ κρίσεως ἐξέταζε σεαυτόν, καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ἐπισκοπῆς εὑρήσεις ἐξιλασμόν. Πρὶν ἀῤῥωστῆσαί σε ταπεινώθητι, καὶ ἐν καιρῷ ἁμαρτημάτων δεῖξον ἐπιστροφήν.

Sirach · 18:20-21

World English Bible

Where does this recognising come from? The text places it in the person before any command arrives: a soul shaped, and given a sense of its own wrong and its own mindfulness. A human being sees clearly into himself, whatever excuses he offers. So the book speaks to a conscience it assumes is already there. That does not make conscience the final judge: people deceive themselves, and the verse says so. It does mean a command comes to someone able to hear it as good.

A question for you

Where did your own sense of right and wrong come from?

If you sayMy family and culture.
ThenMuch of it does, for everyone. The question is whether that is all.
If you saySomething in me, before anyone taught me.
ThenThat is close to what these verses describe, and another Step tests it.
If you sayI do not know.
ThenThat is honest, and a good place to start looking.

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى كَيْفَ تُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ ۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن ۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى ۖ قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًا ثُمَّ ٱدْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًا ۚ وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allāh] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allāh] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself.[107] Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allāh is Exalted in Might and Wise."

Translator's notes

[107] i.e., train them to come to you on command.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:260

Translation

As it is written, “I have made you a father of many nations.” This is in the presence of him whom he believed: God, who gives life to the dead, and calls the things that are not, as though they were. Against hope, Abraham in hope believed, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, “So will your offspring be.” Without being weakened in faith, he didn’t consider his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah’s womb. Yet, looking to the promise of God, he didn’t waver through unbelief, but grew strong through faith, giving glory to God, and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also able to perform.

Original · Ancient Greek

καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε), κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα· ὃς παρʼ ἐλπίδα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου· καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας, εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.

Romans · 4:17-21

World English Bible

One verse seems to close this: He is not questioned about what He does. Does that mean might makes right? Read it beside Abraham, who asks to see how the dead are given life, and is not refused. So the line does not forbid a person's asking. It says no one stands above God to put Him on trial. That leaves one question: if a teaching ever seemed cruel, whom would you trust? The book answers in 7:28: God does not command what is shameful.

A question for you

If a teaching seemed cruel to you, what would you do first?

If you sayAsk whether I have understood it.
ThenThat humility suits every reader, and teachers first.
If you sayAsk who is saying it, and what they gain.
ThenThat is fair too. People have said before that God commanded what is shameful.
If you sayTrust my conscience.
ThenIn this account conscience is a gift, and it can err. Both belong here.
